answer: Scarce audit seats beat expensive puzzles. Each epoch an identity is reviewed by an auditor drawn from a public seed, and any auditor sharing a funding ancestor with the auditee is disqualified. Auditors hold three seats, so every clone a farm creates consumes a seat it cannot fill. As the farm grows, seat scarcity steepens each audit's price, making total attacker cost quadratic in clone count. Saffron trade history or a kernel of peer goodwill cannot buy a seat, and no crystal ball reveals your draw.
